metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_collapse_score: (Mean off-diagonal cosine + 1)/2 for up to 2048 effective ordinary-item embeddings sampled with local seed 42. Approximately 0.5 means mean cosine zero. This measures angular alignment, not recommendation diversity or representation rank. Null for undefined inputs.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-loader-negative score over finite, nonpadding, ordinary-item training positions in at most ten batches. Supplied HSTU features are causal: position t sees sequence[:t+1], not later events.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-order-statistic 10th percentile of sampled pair margins.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of valid sampled pairs with negative score strictly greater than positive score.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of valid sampled pairs with positive-minus-negative score below eps=0.5; depends on score scale.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_category_br: Empty category lists because item categories are unavailable. Position counts remain descriptive; no exposure-adjusted conclusion is supported.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:history_interventions: Frozen fitted-HSTU sensitivity on training targets only; not benchmark validation. Deterministically select up to 32 training users with at least seven events and two distinct endpoints with at least five occupied context events. Training-only counts, transitions and optional title/description TF-IDF define matching; replacement IDs are training-observed, unique, and exclude padding, target and prefix items. Five paired draws reuse identical ordered replacements at disjoint older/recent nonfinal slots. Padding, occupied positions, final item and greatest-nonpadding readout remain fixed. Matching thresholds and sensitivity protocols are stated in protocol; failures and residual imbalance are reported. Each draw uses one shared target plus up to 999 unique uniform negatives excluding the union of all compared histories; this conditional diagnostic catalog never changes the pinned evaluator. With g strictly higher-scoring negatives and e exactly tied negatives, optimistic rank=1+g, pessimistic rank=1+g+e; expected_rank is their midpoint, reciprocal_rank is the exact mean of 1/r over all e+1 positions, and hit10 is the fraction of those positions <=10. Reciprocal midpoint rank is not used. Effects are perturbed-minus-original; positive rank is worse and positive reciprocal rank/hit10 is better. Target-score differences depend on checkpoint scale and must remain category-specific. Definite top10 entry requires original optimistic rank>10 and perturbed pessimistic rank<=10; definite exit requires original pessimistic rank<=10 and perturbed optimistic rank>10. Tie-ambiguous transitions are not counted as definite entry/exit. Identity differences should be zero. Optional random control uses the same replacement list and additional matching checks. Stress control chooses the lowest recent-window transition likelihood among up to sixteen popularity-matched proposals, strictly below original; it does not establish semantic corruption. Draws average within prefixes, then prefixes within users, then users equally. Primary effects use controls present in every retained primary prefix; optional available-case support is explicit in user summaries. Whole-user percentile bootstrap uses 10000 resamples, seed 42, bank 0, retaining overlapping prefixes together; fewer than two users yields null intervals. These descriptive intervals omit training, candidate-generation, matching-selection and replacement-bank uncertainty. Three bank summaries report Monte Carlo/support variability separately; common-user summaries still need not share retained prefixes. Text-complete and missing-text strata are separately reported. Half/double thresholds and k=1 are descriptive and may change support. A four-category macro estimate requires all four identified categories and independent within-category user resampling by the host; do not average interval endpoints, pool user IDs, or macro-average checkpoint-scale target scores. Model sensitivity under these content/location interventions does not identify absolute position, elapsed-time effects, intent, any HSTU component, or generalization. Diagnostic users do not alter the simulator cohort.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:history_intervention_suppo: Effect support follows protocol.effect_support: effects are reported whenever at least one finite draw supports them, including optional controls absent from other prefixes. This replaces the all-prefix control requirement in the history_interventions description. Intervals require at least two supported users and condition on effect-specific retained support. Prefix endpoints identify actual training targets for comparing support across replacement banks; common users alone do not establish common prefixes. Matching details include finite scored draws only; matched_draws_before_score_filter also counts draws subsequently excluded for nonfinite scores. Matching rejection counters count proposal attempts, whereas coverage exclusions count prefixes. Definite entry/exit fields for recent_minus_older are differences between each intervention's entry/exit rates relative to original, not direct older-to-recent transition rates.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:diagnostic_cost: Wall time includes loader access and all probes. CUDA-event elapsed time measures the diagnostic stream interval, including host-induced idle gaps, not kernel-active GPU time. Peak allocated memory is the absolute PyTorch allocation high-water mark after resetting it at audit entry. History cost_counts record actual sequence evaluations, candidate-score calls and scalar candidate scores. CPU GPU statistics are null. No claim of inexpensive auditing is made.
